title: Three Horses
statementMd:
There are three horses living in a horse land: one gray, one white and one gray-and-white. The horses are really amusing animals, which is why they adore special cards. Each of those cards must contain two integers, the first one on top, the second one in the bottom of the card. Let's denote a card with $*a*$ on the top and $*b*$ in the bottom as $(*a*, *b*)$.

Each of the three horses can paint the special cards. If you show an $(*a*, *b*)$ card to the gray horse, then the horse can paint a new $(*a* + 1, *b* + 1)$ card. If you show an $(*a*, *b*)$ card, such that $*a*$ and $*b*$ are even integers, to the white horse, then the horse can paint a new ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/192ec3678af0f5ba2aacda0740464256169e6b63.png) card. If you show two cards $(*a*, *b*)$ and $(*b*, *c*)$ to the gray-and-white horse, then he can paint a new $(*a*, *c*)$ card.

Polycarpus really wants to get $*n*$ special cards $(1, *a*_{1})$, $(1, *a*_{2})$, $...$, $(1, *a*_{*n*})$. For that he is going to the horse land. He can take exactly one $(*x*, *y*)$ card to the horse land, such that $1 ≤ *x* < *y* ≤ *m*$. How many ways are there to choose the card so that he can perform some actions in the horse land and get the required cards?

Polycarpus can get cards from the horses only as a result of the actions that are described above. Polycarpus is allowed to get additional cards besides the cards that he requires.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*, *m*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}, 2 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9})$. The second line contains the sequence of integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ $(2 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$. Note, that the numbers in the sequence can coincide.

The numbers in the lines are separated by single spaces.

## Output

Print a single integer — the answer to the problem.

Please, do not use the `%lld` specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in *C++*. It is preferred to use the `cin`, `cout` streams or the `%I64d` specifier.
statementZhMd:
有三匹马生活在马之国：一匹灰马、一匹白马和一匹灰白相间的马。这些马是非常有趣的动物，因此它们喜欢特殊卡片。每张卡片上必须包含两个整数，第一个写在卡片上方，第二个写在卡片下方。我们将上方写有 $*a*$、下方写有 $*b*$ 的卡片记作 $(*a*, *b*)$。

三匹马中的每一匹都可以绘制特殊卡片。如果将一张 $(*a*, *b*)$ 卡片展示给灰马，那么它可以绘制一张新的 $(*a* + 1, *b* + 1)$ 卡片。如果将一张 $(*a*, *b*)$ 卡片展示给白马，且 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$ 都是偶数，那么它可以绘制一张新的 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/192ec3678af0f5ba2aacda0740464256169e6b63.png) 卡片。如果将两张 $(*a*, *b*)$ 和 $(*b*, *c*)$ 卡片展示给灰白相间的马，那么它可以绘制一张新的 $(*a*, *c*)$ 卡片。

Polycarpus 非常想得到 $*n*$ 张特殊卡片 $(1, *a*_{1})$、$(1, *a*_{2})$、$...$、$(1, *a*_{*n*})$。为此，他要前往马之国。他可以携带恰好一张 $(*x*, *y*)$ 卡片前往马之国，其中 $1 ≤ *x* < *y* ≤ *m*$。有多少种选择卡片的方式，使得他能够在马之国执行若干操作并得到所需的卡片？

Polycarpus 只能通过上述操作从马那里获得卡片。除了所需的卡片外，Polycarpus 也可以获得额外的卡片。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*, *m*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}, 2 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9})$。第二行包含整数序列 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ $(2 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$。注意，序列中的数字可能相同。

每行中的数字之间由单个空格分隔。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——问题的答案。

请不要在 *C++* 中使用 `%lld` 格式说明符读写 64 位整数。建议使用 `cin`、`cout` 流或 `%I64d` 格式说明符。
